mainTopic: A woman who remarried amid conflicting testimony: רב's ruling that she need not leave, שמואל's rule about contradicting a single witness, and why she needs a גט from the second man.
overview: רב ruled that when two witnesses say a husband died and two say he is alive, a woman who remarried need not leave. The גמרא objects that the new couple would owe an אשם תלוי. It answers that she married one of her own witnesses and says 'ברי לי'. Next it asks what רב adds beyond רבי מנחם ברבי יוסי, and gives two versions of how רב relates to him. רבא then challenges רב from a ברייתא about forcing a כהן, and the גמרא gives three answers. רב אשי instead reads רב as saying she stays permitted to her first husband. שמואל adds that she leaves only if she does not contradict a single witness, and the גמרא reconciles this with עולא's rule using רבי נחמיה's majority rule. Finally the גמרא asks why she needs a גט from the second man. רב הונא explains it as a גזירה, and the גמרא defends this using רבי יוסי בן כיפר. A new challenge from the משנה's later clause begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The new husband would owe a doubtful sin-offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב's ruling that she may stay married: the man living with her is in a doubtful case, so he would owe an אשם תלוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the man who lives with her stands obligated to bring an אשם תלוי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב's ruling that the remarried woman does not have to leave. Two witnesses say she is a widow and two say she is still married, so her new marriage might be adultery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם תלוי is brought by someone who may have done a sin whose punishment is כרת. Since one pair of witnesses says she is still married, every time the new husband is with her he faces this doubt. How can רב let a marriage stand that keeps producing a doubtful sin?

keyTerms.meaning: A 'hanging' guilt-offering brought when a person is unsure whether he did a sin that carries כרת
The man who lives with her as a husband
Stands (in a state of), meaning he is in that situation

phrases.english: But the one who has relations with her
stands obligated to bring an uncertain guilt-offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's earlier ruling (stated before this section) that she need not leave.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that if she remarried she does not leave her new husband.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The conflicting witnesses create a real doubt of adultery. That makes the new husband liable for an אשם תלוי, so he should not be allowed to stay with her.

steps.title: She married one of her own witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that רב's case is one where she married one of the witnesses who said her husband died, so the new husband has no doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: The case is where she married one of her witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the challenge by narrowing רב's case. The new husband is one of the witnesses who testified that the first husband died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם תלוי is only owed by someone who is actually in doubt. A witness who saw the death himself knows he is right, so for him there is no doubt and no אשם תלוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Her witnesses, meaning the ones who testified for her that her husband died

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
For example, where she married one of her witnesses.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: כְּגוֹן שֶׁנִּיסֵּת לְאֶחָד מֵעֵדֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב was talking about any new husband, who would be in doubt.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב's case is a husband who was himself a witness to the death, so he has no doubt.

steps.title: But the woman herself is still in doubt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that even if the husband is sure, the woman herself depends on others and so owes an אשם תלוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But she herself stands obligated to bring an אשם תלוי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב ששת's answer. The husband may be certain, but the woman did not see anything herself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman only knows what the witnesses told her, and other witnesses say the opposite. So she is in doubt, and she would owe an אשם תלוי. The problem has only moved from him to her.

keyTerms.meaning: She stands (in that state); the feminine form of קָאֵי

phrases.english: She herself
stands obligated to bring an uncertain guilt-offering!

steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's answer that the husband was her witness.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The woman has no firsthand knowledge, so the doubt and the אשם תלוי still apply to her.

steps.title: She says she is certain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case is where she says 'ברי לי': she is sure her first husband is dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is where she says: 'It is clear to me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the case again. The woman herself claims to be sure that her first husband is dead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once she is personally certain, she is not in doubt either, so she owes no אשם תלוי. Now neither of them is in doubt, and רב's ruling that she may stay makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is clear to me': a claim of personal certainty

phrases.english: Where she says, "It is clear to me."

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The woman is relying only on others and is in doubt.
steps.terutzMaskana: She is personally certain, so she owes no אשם תלוי.

steps.title: Then what is new in רב's ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רב is teaching, since even רבי מנחם ברבי יוסי agrees that she need not leave when the witnesses came after she married.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why say it? Even רבי מנחם ברבי יוסי said his ruling only when the witnesses came and afterward she married. But if she married and afterward the witnesses came, he did not say it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks what רב is adding. It assumes רב's case is one where the opposing witnesses came only after she married, and in that case nobody argues.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מנחם ברבי יוסי is the strict opinion who says she must leave. But even he limits this to when the opposing witnesses came before the marriage. If רב's case is the later-witnesses case, his ruling is something everyone already agrees on.

keyTerms.meaning: Why say it? What is new here?

phrases.english: If so, what is the point of saying it?
Even Rabbi Menachem son of Rabbi Yosei
only said his ruling
when the witnesses came and afterward she married,
phrases.notes: 'The witnesses' here are the second pair, who say the husband is still alive.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל נִיסֵּת וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּאוּ עֵדִים —
phrases.english: but if she married and afterward the witnesses came,
he did not say it.

steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling, now that it has been limited to such a narrow case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רב means witnesses who came after the marriage, even the strict opinion agrees with him, so his statement teaches nothing new.

steps.title: The ברייתא of conflicting witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to prove that רבי מנחם ברבי יוסי's strict view applies only when the witnesses came before the marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: If two say 'he died' and two say 'he did not die', or two say 'she was divorced' and two say 'she was not divorced', she may not marry. But if she married, she does not leave. רבי מנחם ברבי יוסי says: she leaves. רבי מנחם ברבי יוסי said: When do I say she leaves? When the witnesses came and afterward she married. But if she married and afterward the witnesses came, she does not leave!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the source for what the גמרא just said about רבי מנחם ברבי יוסי. The ברייתא shows the מחלוקת and his own limit on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says: if she already married, she stays, because no testimony against her stands unopposed. רבי מנחם ברבי יוסי says she must leave, but he himself explains that this is only when the opposing witnesses came before she married. If they came afterward, he agrees that she stays.

keyTerms.meaning: She may not marry (from the start)
She does not leave (if she already married)

steps.whatToRemember: In a case of two witnesses against two, everyone agrees she should not marry at the start. If she already married and the opposing witnesses came afterward, everyone agrees she stays. The מחלוקת is only when the opposing witnesses came before she married.
steps.confusionAlert: 'לא תנשא' (she may not marry at the start) and 'לא תצא' (if she already married, she need not leave) are two different stages. Do not mix them up.

phrases.english: As it is taught: If two say, "He died,"
and two say, "He did not die,"
or two say, "She was divorced,"
and two say, "She was not divorced" —
this woman may not marry,
and if she married, she does not leave.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מְנַחֵם בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אָמַר: תֵּצֵא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Menachem son of Rabbi Yosei says: She must leave.
Rabbi Menachem son of Rabbi Yosei said:
When do I say she must leave?

phrases.aramaic: בִּזְמַן שֶׁבָּאוּ עֵדִים וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִיסֵּת.
phrases.english: When the witnesses came and afterward she married.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל נִיסֵּת וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּאוּ עֵדִים —
phrases.english: But if she married and afterward the witnesses came,
this woman does not leave!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: שְׁנַיִם אוֹמְרִים מֵת וּשְׁנַיִם אוֹמְרִים לָא מֵת
steps.raayaObject: The claim in step 5 that רבי מנחם ברבי יוסי agrees she stays when the witnesses came after the marriage.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording the מחלוקת between the תנא קמא and רבי מנחם ברבי יוסי, along with his own limit on his ruling.

steps.title: רב means witnesses who came before the marriage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב was talking about witnesses who came before she married, and he rules against רבי מנחם ברבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב spoke, he too meant a case where the witnesses came and afterward she married. He comes to reject the view of רבי מנחם ברבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers 'what is new?' by moving רב's case to the time where there is a real מחלוקת: the opposing witnesses came first, and she married anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now רב is teaching something new. Even when she married after hearing the opposing witnesses, she does not leave. רב sides with the תנא קמא and rejects רבי מנחם ברבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude, meaning to reject another opinion

phrases.english: When Rav spoke, too,

phrases.aramaic: בִּזְמַן שֶׁבָּאוּ עֵדִים וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִיסֵּת.
phrases.english: it was when the witnesses came and afterward she married.
This is to exclude the view of Rabbi Menachem son of Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָאָמַר רַב נָמֵי, בִּזְמַן שֶׁבָּאוּ עֵדִים וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִיסֵּת
steps.terutzResolutionType: Placing רב's ruling inside the מחלוקת
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב spoke about witnesses who came after the marriage, where everyone agrees.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב spoke about witnesses who came before the marriage, and he rules like the תנא קמא against רבי מנחם ברבי יוסי.

steps.title: Another version: רב agrees with רבי מנחם ברבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: A second version reads רב as speaking only about witnesses who came after she married. If they came first, she must leave, like רבי מנחם ברבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: The reason is that she married and afterward the witnesses came. But if the witnesses came and afterward she married, she must leave. Whose view is this? רבי מנחם ברבי יוסי's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of how רב's ruling was understood. In this version, רב fits with רבי מנחם ברבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רב's leniency depends on the order of events. She stays only if she married before the opposing witnesses appeared. If they came first, she must leave, and that is exactly the view of רבי מנחם ברבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say: introduces another version

steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of רב. In the first, רב says she stays even if the witnesses came first, against רבי מנחם ברבי יוסי. In the second, רב says she stays only if the witnesses came after she married, like רבי מנחם ברבי יוסי.

phrases.english: And some say:

phrases.aramaic: טַעְמָא דְּנִיסֵּת וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּאוּ עֵדִים,
phrases.english: The reason is that she married and afterward the witnesses came,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בָּאוּ עֵדִים וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִיסֵּת — תֵּצֵא.
phrases.english: but if the witnesses came and afterward she married, she must leave.
In accordance with whom? With Rabbi Menachem son of Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמַר: טַעְמָא דְּנִיסֵּת וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּאוּ עֵדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different reading of רב from the one in step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב rejects רבי מנחם ברבי יוסי.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב's ruling is limited to witnesses who came after the marriage, which fits רבי מנחם ברבי יוסי.

steps.title: רבא quotes a teaching about forcing a כהן
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a ברייתא: if a כהן does not want to keep the rules of כהונה, בית דין forces him, based on the פסוק 'וקדשתו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objects: How do we know that if a כהן does not want to obey, we force him? The פסוק says 'And you shall make him holy': even against his will.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a challenge against רב by quoting a ברייתא. This step is setting up the attack. The actual argument comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא teaches that בית דין does not wait for a כהן to separate from a forbidden woman on his own; they force him. On its own this is not yet a problem for רב. רבא is about to show why it is one.

keyTerms.meaning: push him / force him (by בית דין)
'and you shall make him holy' (ויקרא כא:ח)

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection:
From where do we know that if he (a Kohen) does not want to, we force him?
The verse says: "And you shall make him holy",
even against his will.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the earlier question about what רב teaches, רבא brings a new source that seems to argue with רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that a woman who married based on two witnesses need not leave when two others contradict them
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says בית דין forces a כהן to separate. The next step will show it must be talking about a disputed case like רב's.

steps.title: Proving the teaching must contradict רב
steps.stepSummary: רבא shows that the ברייתא cannot mean an obvious case. So it must mean a case where she married one of her witnesses and says 'ברי לי'. Even then we force him, so we do remove her, against רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If she did not marry one of her witnesses and does not say 'I am sure', do we even need a פסוק to tell us to force him? Rather, it must be where she married one of her witnesses and says 'I am sure', and still the ברייתא says we force him. So we do take her away from him!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now makes the challenge land. He shows that the ברייתא has to be talking about רב's exact type of case, and it says to separate them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a simple case where the marriage is clearly forbidden, nobody needs to be taught that בית דין steps in. So the ברייתא must be teaching something new: even in the strongest case for the couple (she married her own witness and is sure), we separate them. That directly opposes רב, who said she need not leave.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the case? (how do we picture it)
does this need to be said? (it is obvious)

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the ברייתא openly talks about witnesses. He is arguing that the only case worth teaching must be רב's kind of case.

phrases.english: What is the case?
If you say that she did not marry one of her witnesses
and she does not say "I am sure,"
does it need to be said that we force him?
Rather, is it not where she married one of her witnesses,
and she says "I am sure,"
and yet it teaches that we force him.
This shows that we remove her from him!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי, אִילֵּימָא דְּלָא נִיסֵּת לְאֶחָד מֵעֵדֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge that step 9 set up by working out what case the ברייתא must mean.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling, as explained in step 4 (she married one of her witnesses and says ברי לי)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא would be pointless in an obvious case, so it must mean רב's case. There it says to separate them, while רב says she stays.

steps.title: Prohibitions of כהונה are different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that rules of כהונה are stricter, so the ברייתא does not show anything about a regular case like רב's.
steps.simpleTranslation: A prohibition of כהונה is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer: the ברייתא is about a כהן, and כהונה rules are treated more strictly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא assumed that the ברייתא's ruling teaches us about every marriage. This answer limits it to כהנים, where even a doubt is treated as forbidden. רב's ruling for an ordinary marriage stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: a prohibition that applies to a כהן

phrases.english: A prohibition of the priesthood is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge from step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: כהונה versus an ordinary marriage
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא about the כהן shows how we rule in every marriage like this.
steps.terutzMaskana: כהונה is stricter. The ברייתא tells us nothing about רב's ordinary case.

steps.title: Forcing him only with clear witnesses
steps.stepSummary: Second answer: 'we force him' means only when clear witnesses testify before the marriage, not to break up a marriage that has already happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: what does 'we force him' mean? We force him through witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer by reading the word דפנו differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here, 'forcing' means that בית דין stops the marriage beforehand when witnesses clearly show she is forbidden. It does not say to remove a wife he has already married. So there is no clash with רב, who talks about a woman already married.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you want, say (another answer)

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
What does "we force him" mean? We force him through witnesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, independent answer to the challenge in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading a word in the ברייתא differently
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Forcing' means taking her away even after she has married.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Forcing' means stopping the marriage beforehand when there are witnesses.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי מנחם ברבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: Third answer: the ברייתא is about witnesses who came before she married, and it follows רבי מנחם ברבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: it is where the witnesses came first and afterward she married, and it follows רבי מנחם ברבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third answer: the ברייתא is talking about a different timing and follows a strict opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the contradicting witnesses came before the wedding, רבי מנחם ברבי יוסי holds that she must leave, and the ברייתא can follow his view. רב, in step 7's version, rules like the תנא קמא who argues with him, so a ברייתא that follows רבי מנחם ברבי יוסי is no challenge to רב.

keyTerms.meaning: when the witnesses came and afterward she married

steps.whatToRemember: There are three answers to רבא. (1) כהונה is stricter. (2) 'Forcing' means stopping the marriage beforehand with witnesses. (3) The ברייתא is about witnesses who came first, following רבי מנחם ברבי יוסי.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
it is where witnesses came and afterward she married,
and it follows Rabbi Menachem son of Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִבָּעֵית אֵימָא: כְּשֶׁבָּאוּ עֵדִים וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִיסֵּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to step 10, built on the ברייתא of רבי מנחם ברבי יוסי from step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Placing the ברייתא in a different case and linking it to a known opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about the same timing as רב's case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about witnesses who came before the marriage and follows רבי מנחם ברבי יוסי. רב follows the תנא קמא who argues with him (step 7's version).

steps.title: רב אשי's new reading of רב
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that רב's 'she need not leave' means she does not lose her permission to her first husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי says: What does 'she need not leave' that רב said mean? She does not leave her first permission, meaning she stays permitted to her first husband.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a brand-new explanation of רב's words, different from everything the גמרא assumed until now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, everyone read רב as saying she may stay with her second husband. רב אשי reads it as saying she keeps her permission to return to her first husband. Since she married on the word of proper witnesses, she was not acting on purpose. On this reading רבא's challenge falls away, because רב never said she stays with the second husband.

keyTerms.meaning: her first permission (to her first husband)

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי does not say she stays with her second husband. He is talking about her being allowed back to her first husband.
steps.whyThisMatters: This reverses how רב's ruling was understood: the second marriage is not kept, but the woman is not punished by being forbidden to her first husband.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi says:
What does "she need not leave" that Rav said mean?
She does not leave her first permission.
phrases.notes: He means she is still allowed to go back to her first husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אוֹמֵר: מַאי ״לֹא תֵּצֵא״ דְּקָאָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a completely different reading of רב, which also removes רבא's challenge.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב's 'she need not leave' means she stays permitted to her first husband, not that she stays with the second.

steps.title: רב already said this once
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to רב אשי's reading: רב already ruled elsewhere that she may return to her first husband, so why say it twice?
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב already said this once! For we learned in a משנה: if she married without permission, she is allowed to go back to him. And רב הונא said in the name of רב: that is the הלכה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אשי's explanation from Step 14. If רב only meant 'she does not lose her permission to her first husband,' he already said that once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי read רב's words 'she need not leave' as 'she stays permitted to her first husband.' But רב already ruled the same thing on a משנה about a woman who married without permission. A sage does not usually repeat the same ruling, so the reading looks doubtful.

phrases.english: But Rav already said it one time,
as we learned: If she married without permission —
phrases.notes: Without permission of the בית דין. She married based on witnesses alone.

phrases.english: she is permitted to return to him.
And Rav Huna said that Rav said:
That is the halakha!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's interpretation in Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's reading of רב's 'she need not leave'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that is the meaning, רב would be repeating a ruling he already gave on a משנה, which is unlikely.

steps.title: One ruling was inferred from the other
steps.stepSummary: רב did not say both rulings openly. He said one, and the other was learned from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: One was stated by inference from the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the repetition problem. רב only said one ruling outright, and the second was worked out from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no real repetition. Only one of the two statements is רב's own words. The other is a conclusion that students drew from it, so רב אשי's reading still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: by inference, as something included in

phrases.english: One was stated by inference from the other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of how the statements were transmitted
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב explicitly said the same ruling twice.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב said only one ruling. The other was derived from it, so nothing is repeated.
steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי's reading of רב survives: 'she need not leave' means she keeps her permission to her first husband.

steps.title: שמואל: she leaves only if she does not contradict
steps.stepSummary: שמואל limits the ruling. She must leave only when she does not deny the witness who says her husband is alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: They only taught this when she does not contradict him. But if she contradicts him, she need not leave.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל adds a new limit. The rule that she must leave applies only if she stays quiet and does not deny the witness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The witness says the first husband is alive. If the woman says 'that is not true,' her denial counts, and she can stay with her second husband. If she stays silent, she must leave.

keyTerms.meaning: she does not have to leave

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
They taught only when she does not contradict him,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the witness who says her first husband is still alive.

phrases.english: but if she contradicts him — she need not leave.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא מַכְחַשְׁתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new line: a limit on when she must leave.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: She leaves only if she does not contradict the witness. If she contradicts him, she stays.

steps.title: What case is שמואל talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case שמואל means. It cannot be two witnesses, because her denial would not matter against two.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with? If you say two witnesses, what difference does it make if she contradicts them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what kind of case שמואל means. It first rules out a case of two witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two valid witnesses are full testimony. A woman's denial cannot cancel it. So her contradicting them could not change anything, and שמואל must mean a different case.

keyTerms.meaning: what case are we dealing with?
what of it? what difference does it make?

phrases.english: With what are we dealing?
If we say with two witnesses,
when she contradicts him, what of it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what case Step 17 is about.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether שמואל's case involves two witnesses or one.

steps.title: It must be one witness, so silence means she leaves
steps.stepSummary: The case must involve one witness. That gives an inference: if she stays silent, she must leave.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is with one witness. The reason she stays is that she contradicts him. But if she is silent, she must leave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that שמואל means a case of one witness. From his words it infers that if she says nothing, she must leave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only one witness says the husband is alive, so her denial can stand against him. Read the other way, if she does not deny it, his single word is enough to make her leave. This inference sets up the next challenge.

phrases.english: Rather, with one witness,
the reason is that she contradicts him,
but if she is silent — she must leave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 18 and draws an inference.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is one witness. So if she is silent, she leaves.

steps.title: עולא: one trusted witness counts like two
steps.stepSummary: עולא taught that when the Torah trusts one witness, he counts as two, and one later witness cannot override him. So why should a single witness make her leave?
steps.simpleTranslation: But עולא said: Wherever the Torah trusted one witness, it is as if there are two here, and the word of one has no weight against two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the inference of Step 19 using a rule of עולא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first witness, who said the husband died, was trusted by Torah law, so he counts like two. One later witness who says the husband is alive is only one against 'two.' He should not be able to make her leave, even if she stays silent.

keyTerms.meaning: it is as if there are two here

phrases.english: But didn't Ulla say:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁהֶאֱמִינָה תּוֹרָה עֵד אֶחָד,
phrases.english: Wherever the Torah trusted one witness,
here it is like two,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל אֶחָד בִּמְקוֹם שְׁנַיִם!
phrases.english: and the words of one have no weight against two!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר עוּלָּא: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁהֶאֱמִינָה תּוֹרָה עֵד אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the inference of Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that if she is silent, a single witness makes her leave
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By עולא's rule, the first trusted witness counts as two, so one later witness cannot override him.

steps.title: The case involves disqualified witnesses, like רבי נחמיה
steps.stepSummary: The case is about witnesses who are not fully valid (פסולי עדות), and it follows רבי נחמיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? Witnesses who are disqualified from testimony, and it follows רבי נחמיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers עולא's challenge. The case involves פסולי עדות, so עולא's rule does not decide it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא's rule works with fully valid testimony. Here the people saying the husband is alive are disqualified, so they are counted one by one, and the majority view decides. רבי נחמיה's source comes next.

phrases.english: Here, with what are we dealing —
with those disqualified from testimony,
and in line with Rabbi Nechemya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 20.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case involves valid witnesses, so עולא's 'one counts as two' should apply.
steps.terutzMaskana: The witnesses are פסולי עדות, so the majority of opinions decides, as רבי נחמיה holds.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה: follow the majority of opinions
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי נחמיה: where the Torah trusts one witness, go after the majority of opinions, and two women against one man count like two men against one man.
steps.simpleTranslation: As taught in a ברייתא: רבי נחמיה says: Wherever the Torah trusted one witness, follow the majority of opinions. And they made two women against one man like two men against one man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רבי נחמיה's view, which supports the answer in Step 21.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With disqualified witnesses, we count heads, and the side with more people wins. So if two say 'alive' and one says 'dead,' she leaves. If she contradicts them, her voice joins the other side, and the majority no longer forces her out. That explains why שמואל says silence matters.
steps.whatToRemember: With disqualified witnesses, רבי נחמיה says to count heads. Her own denial can change the count, which is why שמואל says her silence or denial decides.

phrases.english: As it is taught, Rabbi Nechemya says:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁהֶאֱמִינָה תּוֹרָה עֵד אֶחָד —
phrases.english: Wherever the Torah trusted one witness —
follow the majority of opinions.
And they made two women against one man
like two men against one man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for רבי נחמיה, cited in Step 21.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that the case follows רבי נחמיה's majority rule for disqualified witnesses

steps.title: A second answer: עולא's rule applies only when a valid witness came first
steps.stepSummary: A second answer to עולא's challenge. If a fully valid עד אחד testified first, even a hundred women against him count only as one witness. Our case is where a woman testified first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can answer this way. Whenever one valid witness came first, even a hundred women against him count as one witness. But here the case is where a woman came first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another answer to עולא's question from step 20. It says עולא's rule only applies when the first witness was a fully valid man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא said one trusted witness counts like two, so a later single witness cannot overturn him. That is true only when the first witness was a כשר man; then even many women cannot outweigh him. In our case the first witness was a woman, so later witnesses who disagree with her can outweigh her.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say: introduces a second, different answer

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל הֵיכָא דַּאֲתָא עֵד אֶחָד כָּשֵׁר מֵעִיקָּרָא,
phrases.english: Anywhere that one valid witness came first,
even a hundred women
are like one witness.
Here, what are we dealing with?
Where a woman came first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to עולא's challenge, in place of the answer from steps 21-22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of עולא's rule by redefining the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: עולא's rule seemed to mean any first single witness can never be overturned.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule protects only a first witness who is a valid man. A woman who testified first can be outweighed by a majority.

steps.title: Rewording רבי נחמיה's teaching to fit the second answer
steps.stepSummary: Under this answer, רבי נחמיה's ברייתא is reworded. Two women against one woman are like two men against one man. But two women against one valid man are only half against half.
steps.simpleTranslation: Reword רבי נחמיה's teaching like this. רבי נחמיה says: wherever the Torah trusts one witness, follow the majority. Two women against one woman count like two men against one man. But two women against one man are half against half.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rewords the ברייתא from step 22 so that it matches the new answer from step 23.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the old wording, two women outweighed one man. That clashes with the new answer, which says a valid man who testified first cannot be outweighed by women. So the ברייתא now says the majority wins only women against women. Two women against a valid man are an even split.

keyTerms.meaning: Like half and half; evenly split

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions of the ברייתא. In step 22 two women beat one man. In this reworded version they only tie with one man, and they win only against one woman.

phrases.english: And reword the teaching of Rabbi Nechemya like this:
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא quoted in step 22, now changed to fit the new answer.

phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya says:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁהֶאֱמִינָה תּוֹרָה עֵד אֶחָד —
phrases.english: Wherever the Torah trusted one witness,
follow the majority of opinions,
and they made two women against one woman
like two men against one man.
But two women against one man
are like half and half.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adjusts the supporting ברייתא so that it matches the second answer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא said two women outweigh one man.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two women outweigh only one woman. Against one valid man they are an even split.
steps.whatToRemember: Under the second answer, a valid man who testified first holds his ground against women. Only a woman who testified first can be outweighed by two women who disagree with her.

steps.title: Why does she need a גט from the second husband?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says she needs a גט from both men. A גט from the first husband makes sense. But her bond with the second man was never a real marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says she needs a גט from this one and from that one. From the first husband, fine. But why from the second? It was only illicit relations!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. It asks why the second man, whose marriage never took effect, has to give her a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her first husband was alive, so she was still a married woman. That means קידושין to the second man could not take effect. Without a real marriage, a גט should not be needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Mere illicit relations, not a marriage

phrases.english: She needs a get from this one and from that one.
Granted, from the first she needs a get,
but from the second, why?
It is merely illicit relations!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא מֵרִאשׁוֹן תִּבְעֵי גֵּט, אֶלָּא מִשֵּׁנִי אַמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from a different line of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that she needs a גט from the second man
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גט ends a marriage. Since no marriage with the second man ever took effect, there is nothing for a גט to end.

steps.title: רב הונא: a rabbinic decree so people will not get the wrong idea
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says the second גט is a rabbinic גזירה. Without it, people might think the first husband divorced her and the second truly married her. They would then see a married woman leaving her husband with no גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: it is a decree. Otherwise people might say the first man divorced her and the second married her, and they would see a married woman leaving without a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the question in step 25. He explains that the second גט is required by the Rabbis, not by Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Onlookers do not know the full story. To them it looks like a real second marriage. If she left the second man with no גט, they would wrongly learn that a married woman can leave without one. The Rabbis require a גט to prevent that mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made to prevent a mistake

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
It is a decree, lest they say
this one divorced and that one married,
and a married woman would be found
leaving without a get.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יֹאמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rabbinic decree based on how things look to others
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No גט should be needed, because the second marriage was never real.
steps.terutzMaskana: A גט is required by the Rabbis so people will not think a married woman can leave without one.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the Rabbis sometimes require a גט even where Torah law needs none, to protect people's understanding of marriage law.

steps.title: Challenge from the later clause: a woman who was only engaged may go back
steps.stepSummary: A later clause of the משנה says that if she only got engaged to the second man, she may go back to her first husband, with no גט from the second. By רב הונא's logic, people should think the same mistake there.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the later clause teaches: they told her your husband died, she got engaged, then her husband came. She may go back to him. There too, people should say the first divorced her and the second engaged her, and a married woman is leaving without a גט!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא's reason from another part of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the later clause she was only engaged to the second man, yet she may return to her first husband with no גט from the second. רב הונא's worry should apply there too: people might think the engagement was real and see her leave the second man with no גט. So why was no גזירה made there?

keyTerms.meaning: She is permitted to go back to him

phrases.english: If so,
the latter clause that teaches:
They said to her, "Your husband died,"
and she became betrothed, and afterward her husband came,
she is permitted to go back to him.
There too, let us say:
this one divorced and that one betrothed,

phrases.aramaic: וְנִמְצֵאת אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ יוֹצְאָה שֶׁלֹּא בַּגֵּט!
phrases.english: and a married woman would be found leaving without a get!
phrases.notes: Here the "married woman" is her bond to the second man, which onlookers would think was real.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב הונא's answer from step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's reason for the second גט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same worry applies to the case of engagement, yet the משנה lets her return to her first husband with no גט from the second man. So the worry cannot be the real reason.

steps.title: Even after an engagement she needs a גט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers step 27. Even in the engagement case, she really does need a גט from the second man before going back to her first husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, she does need a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 27. It says the engagement case also needs a גט from the second man, so רב הונא's גזירה still holds there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 read the משנה's engagement clause as letting her go back to her first husband with no גט from the second man. The גמרא now says that is not what the משנה means. She does need a גט from the second man, and only then may she return. This fits רב הונא's reasoning that people might mistake the situation.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually. It marks a fuller or corrected reading of a case.
She needs a bill of divorce

phrases.english: Really, she does need a bill of divorce.
phrases.notes: He means a גט from the second man, the one she was only engaged to.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 27 by rereading the משנה's engagement clause.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה: 'she may return' is said only after she gets a גט from the second man.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The engagement clause lets her return to her first husband with no גט from the second man, which goes against רב הונא's גזירה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even in the engagement case she needs a גט from the second man, so רב הונא's גזירה applies there too.

steps.title: Then it looks like he is taking back his divorced wife
steps.stepSummary: If she gets a גט from the second man, people will think the first husband divorced her too. Then it would look like he is remarrying his divorced wife after she was engaged to another man.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, we find this man taking back his divorced wife after she was engaged to someone else!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. Giving a גט in the engagement case creates a new appearance problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's whole worry was that people would think the first husband divorced her. If we require a גט from the second man, onlookers will think she was the first husband's divorced wife who then got engaged to another man. When she goes back to the first husband, it looks like the banned case of a man remarrying his former wife after she was with someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: If so. This opens a challenge built on the answer just given.
A man who takes back his divorced wife

phrases.english: If so,
we find this one taking back his divorced wife after she was engaged to another!
phrases.notes: The ban on taking back a divorced wife who was with someone else comes from דברים 24:4.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, נִמְצָא זֶה מַחֲזִיר גְּרוּשָׁתוֹ מִשֶּׁנִּתְאָרְסָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 28 by using רב הונא's own 'people will think' reasoning against it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 28 that the engagement case needs a גט from the second man
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If people think the first husband divorced her, then her going back to him looks like a man taking back his divorced wife after she was engaged to another man. That would itself look forbidden.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי יוסי בן כיפר
steps.stepSummary: The משנה holds like רבי יוסי בן כיפר. He says a divorced wife may not go back to her first husband after full marriage to another man. After only an engagement, she may.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows רבי יוסי בן כיפר, who said: after marriage, she is forbidden; after engagement, she is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the משנה follows רבי יוסי בן כיפר. According to him, even what people might think here is not forbidden at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוסי בן כיפר, the ban on taking back a divorced wife applies only if she was fully married (נישואין) to another man. If she was only engaged (אירוסין), the first husband may take her back. So even if onlookers think she was divorced and then engaged, what they imagine is still allowed. Nothing bad results from their mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: Engagement, the first stage of marriage

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of 'forbidden' here. רב הונא's גזירה is about what people might wrongly think. רבי יוסי בן כיפר is about the actual law of מחזיר גרושתו. His view means that what people would think in the engagement case is a permitted situation anyway.
steps.whatToRemember: In the engagement case she needs a גט from the second man, because of רב הונא's גזירה. She may still go back to her first husband, because רבי יוסי בן כיפר limits the ban on taking back a divorced wife to cases of full marriage.

phrases.english: It follows Rabbi Yosei ben Kippar, who said:
from marriage, she is forbidden,
phrases.notes: He means a divorced woman who then fully married another man may not go back to her first husband.

phrases.english: from engagement, she is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 29 by tying the משנה to a תנא for whom the imagined situation is allowed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Tying the משנה to a specific תנא's opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Requiring a גט makes it look like the first husband is breaking the ban on taking back his divorced wife.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יוסי בן כיפר, taking back a divorced wife after she was only engaged to another man is allowed, so the appearance causes no problem.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the גמרא can keep one rabbinic worry (רב הונא's גזירה) without creating a second one. It does this by picking the opinion under which the second worry does not arise.

steps.title: A new challenge from the later clause of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a new challenge based on a later clause (סיפא) of the משנה, which begins with 'even though.' The challenge continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: But from the fact that the later clause teaches: 'Even though...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It begins quoting a later clause of the משנה in order to raise a new difficulty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'from the fact that it teaches' signal an inference from the wording of a later clause of the משנה. The quote is cut off at the end of this amud, and the clause and its difficulty continue on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: From the fact that it teaches. This introduces an inference from the wording of a text.
The later clause of a משנה or ברייתא

phrases.english: But from the fact that the later clause teaches:
Even though
phrases.notes: The quote is cut off here and continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After closing the engagement question, the גמרא turns to a new difficulty based on the משנה's later clause.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 28 that, even in the engagement case, she needs a גט from the second man (the details continue on the next amud)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An inference from the wording of a later clause of the משנה, which begins with 'even though.' The full argument continues on the next amud.
